title: Congruence mod n
short: a ≡ b (mod n) when n ∣ (a − b), that is, when a and b leave the same remainder on division by n.
trouble: Students drop the sign of a negative number and write −3 ≡ 3 (mod 7). In fact −3 ≡ 4 (mod 7).

blocks.html: Clocks, calendars and odd/even all ignore multiples of some fixed number: 15 hours after 11 o'clock is 2 o'clock, because only the remainder mod 12 matters. Gauss turned this into an algebra with one new symbol, and it is the language of the rest of this course.

Definition. Let $n \ge 1$. Integers $a$ and $b$ are congruent mod $n$, written $$a \equiv b \pmod{n},$$ when $n \mid (a - b)$. The number $n$ is the modulus. For example $38 \equiv 3 \pmod{7}$, because $38 - 3 = 35 = 7 \cdot 5$.

Congruent means "same remainder". Use the division algorithm: $a = nq + r$ and $b = nq' + r'$ with $0 \le r, r' < n$. Then $a - b = n(q - q') + (r - r')$, so $n \mid (a - b)$ exactly when $n \mid (r - r')$. But $r - r'$ lies strictly between $-n$ and $n$, and the only multiple of $n$ there is $0$. So $a \equiv b \pmod{n}$ exactly when $r = r'$.

Congruence mod $n$ is an equivalence relation: $a \equiv a$; if $a \equiv b$ then $b \equiv a$; if $a \equiv b$ and $b \equiv c$ then $a \equiv c$ (add $a - b$ and $b - c$). Its classes, the residue classes, are the $n$ sets of integers with remainder $0, 1, \dots, n - 1$. The least nonnegative residue of $a$ is its remainder, the one representative from $0$ to $n - 1$.

blocks.name: nt-clock

opts.task: Change add to $-10$, then to $11$. Where do you land each time?

blocks.cap: Mod 7 the number line wraps around a clock with 7 points. Going back 3 from 0 lands on 4, so $-3 \equiv 4 \pmod{7}$; the gray labels outside show the negative names of each point.

blocks.title: Least nonnegative residues
blocks.q: Find the least nonnegative residues of $38$ and $-3$ mod $7$.
steps: Many numbers name the same class: $38 \equiv 3 \equiv 10 \equiv -4 \pmod{7}$.

blocks.title: Odd squares mod 8
blocks.q: Show that the square of an odd number is $\equiv 1 \pmod{8}$, using classes mod 8.
steps: So every odd square is $\equiv 1 \pmod{8}$ (squares of congruent numbers are congruent, as the next lesson shows).

blocks.html: Dropping the sign: "$-3 \equiv 3 \pmod{7}$." Test it with the definition: $-3 - 3 = -6$, and $7 \nmid -6$. On the clock, $-3$ is three steps back from 0, which is the point $4$: $-3 \equiv 4 \pmod{7}$. To reduce a negative number, add multiples of $n$ until you land between $0$ and $n - 1$.
$a \equiv b \pmod{n}$ means $n \mid (a - b)$, which is the same as "$a$ and $b$ leave the same remainder." Every integer is congruent to exactly one of $0, 1, \dots, n - 1$.
